newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish shares close lower, Skanska deal in focus.
newsitem.headline: Swedish shares close lower, Skanska deal in focus.

text.p: Swedish shares ended lower on Monday, depressed from the outset by a weaker U.S. market and falls in Asia.
Stockholm general index fell 1.1 percent to 2,603.68. Turnover hit 10.74 billion crowns, but large stakes in tool maker/engineer Sandvik and power group Sydkraft accounted for seven billion crowns.

"We had two interesting deals today but it's still a very boring bourse and will probably stay that way for a while," a broker said. He added that trade will remain quiet as nervousness on the U.S. economy persists.
The day's main story was construction group Skanska's news it selling all its stake in engineer Sandvik.

Investor Industrivarden and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell are buying over half of Skanska's 10 billion crown holding while Skanska was to use over 23 million shares to guarantee a four billion crown share redemption by Sandvik.
Skanska ended six crowns higher at 330. Industrivarden dropped five to 382 while Sandvik lost 6.5 to 187 crowns.
Heavyweight telecom group Ericsson slipped three crowns to 245.5 and drugs major Astra fell 5.5 to 337.5.
